transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As you all know, Weld Cell 4 stopped this morning after its coolant-system alarm activated during the 480 chassis bracket run. The external surfaces look normal and the visual inspection didn't find obvious weld defects, but that doesn't mean we're clear to restart. Per our plant restart procedure, I need to conduct a pre-restart check-in with both quality and maintenance before I can authorize this cell to run again. So let's get into it -- I need to hear from maintenance on what they've found regarding the coolant alarm, and from quality on whether we have any concerns about the brackets that were in process. What are we looking at?

transcript.text: Mara, I need to flag a serious quality concern before we go any further. This morning I completed a laboratory review of retained samples from the last two hours of the run. I found lack of fusion in 8 of 20 weld cross-sections. The results aren't entered in the batch record yet, but per our quality containment rule, we need to hold exactly 240 brackets from that production window and perform destructive validation on exactly 12 brackets after the cell is corrected. This is a significant finding that needs to be addressed before we can consider restart.
